nodes.text: Microarray Normalization Method Comparison (ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow). Bioc Workflow ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow analog: read raw microarray CEL/IDAT files, normalize with multiple methods (RMA, vsn, lumi, ComBat), compare normalization quality via PCA and variance estimation. For normalization quality comparison and method selection ONLY — NOT for differential expression statistical testing. For differential expression analysis from a normalized microarray count matrix, use nf-core/differentialabundance.

Germline variant calling on WES data for rare disease diagnosis | germline short-variant calling from paired-end whole-exome sequencing FASTQ (alignment, duplicate marking, base quality recalibration, HaplotypeCaller) → annotated, filtered VCF of rare SNVs/indels

RNA-seq processing with expression and splicing outlier detection for rare disease functional evidence | RNA-seq alignment and quantification from FASTQ with aberrant expression (OUTRIDER-style) and aberrant splicing (FRASER-style) outlier detection → per-gene expression outliers and splicing outliers

Integrate WES rare variants with RNA-seq expression/splicing outliers to prioritize causal rare disease variants | integration of rare germline variants (VCF) with transcriptomic outlier evidence — cross-modal variant prioritization combining population frequency, predicted pathogenicity, and RNA-level functional evidence → ranked candidate causal variants/genes for rare disease diagnosis

RNA-seq Differential Transcript Usage (rnaseqDTU). Bioc Workflow `rnaseqDTU` analog: quantify transcripts (Salmon), import via tximport, then + DEXSeq + stageR for differential transcript usage with FDR control.

Germline variant calling and annotation from WES data for rare disease workup | germline short-variant calling from whole-exome sequencing FASTQ or BAM (alignment, duplicate marking, base recalibration, HaplotypeCaller, VEP annotation) → annotated VCF with rare disease-relevant variants

RNA-seq analysis for aberrant expression and splicing to support rare disease diagnosis | bulk RNA-seq alignment and quantification from FASTQ (STAR/Salmon), followed by aberrant expression and aberrant splicing analysis (e.g., OUTRIDER/FRASER or DROP pipeline) → per-gene aberrancy z-scores and outlier calls for rare disease candidate prioritization

Integrate WES variant calls and RNA-seq aberrant expression/splicing results for rare disease diagnosis | integration of germline WES variant calls (annotated VCF) with RNA-seq aberrant expression and splicing outlier calls — cross-reference variants with expression outliers, prioritize candidate genes showing both coding and regulatory/expressed evidence → ranked candidate gene list for rare disease diagnosis

RNA-seq + Epigenomic Integration (fluentGenomics). Bioc Workflow `fluentGenomics` analog: integrate RNA-seq differential genes with ATAC-seq accessibility regions and ChIP-seq TF binding peaks, link peaks to genes via + .

RNA-seq Differential Transcript Usage (rnaseqDTU). Bioc Workflow `rnaseqDTU` analog: quantify transcripts (Salmon), import via tximport, then + DEXSeq + stageR for differential transcript usage with FDR control.

RNA-seq + Epigenomic Integration (fluentGenomics). Bioc Workflow `fluentGenomics` analog: integrate RNA-seq differential genes with ATAC-seq accessibility regions and ChIP-seq TF binding peaks, link peaks to genes via + .

RNA-seq differential expression analysis — identify differentially expressed genes between conditions from bulk RNA-seq FASTQ or count matrix | differential gene expression on bulk RNA-seq data (DESeq2/edgeR negative-binomial model), two-group or multi-group comparison → per-gene log2 fold change, adjusted p-values, and normalized counts

ATAC-seq accessibility analysis — call open chromatin peaks and identify differentially accessible regions between conditions from ATAC-seq FASTQ | open chromatin peak calling and differential accessibility from paired-end ATAC-seq FASTQ (alignment with Bowtie2, duplicate removal, MACS2 narrow peak calling, DiffBind/DESeq2 differential accessibility) → consensus peak set and per-region accessibility scores

ChIP-seq TF binding analysis — call transcription factor binding peaks and identify differential binding sites from ChIP-seq FASTQ | transcription factor binding peak calling and differential binding from paired-end ChIP-seq FASTQ (alignment, duplicate removal, MACS2 narrow peak calling, DiffBind differential binding) → consensus TF binding peak set and per-peak binding intensity scores

Integrate RNA-seq differential genes with ATAC-seq accessibility regions and ChIP-seq TF binding peaks — link peaks to genes and identify regulatory relationships | integration of three quantitative omics layers (RNA-seq differential expression, ATAC-seq differential accessibility, ChIP-seq differential TF binding) — peak-to-gene linkage via genomic proximity / correlation across samples, construction of regulatory element–target gene networks, identification of concordant accessibility + expression + TF binding events → integrated regulatory network and ranked peak-gene-TF associations

Guide RNA assignment from Perturb-seq single-cell CRISPR screen data — capture sgRNA barcodes from scRNA-seq reads or direct guide capture library, assign each cell its targeting guide(s), and generate a cell × guide assignment matrix | sgRNA guide-to-cell assignment from single-cell CRISPR screen (Perturb-seq) data — parse guide capture barcodes from scRNA-seq FASTQ or 10x feature barcoding library, demultiplex guide identities, assign guides to cells with UMI counting → cell × guide assignment table with quality metrics (guide UMI counts, assignment confidence, multiplet rate)

Hit calling from Perturb-seq screen — identify perturbations with significant transcriptional phenotypic effects using differential expression or perturbation effect magnitude testing across guide-targeted cell groups vs non-targeting controls | differential perturbation analysis / hit calling on single-cell CRISPR screen data — compare transcriptional profiles of guide-targeted cells vs non-targeting control cells, compute perturbation effect scores (magnitude, differential expression, FDR-adjusted p-values) → ranked list of significant perturbations (hits) with effect sizes and per-gene perturbation signatures

Perturbation state embedding using scVI / scANVI — learn latent representations of perturbation states from the Perturb-seq single-cell expression data, integrating batch correction and semi-supervised cell-type annotation to visualize and compare perturbation effects in latent space | latent embedding of single-cell perturbation states using variational inference (scVI for unsupervised batch-corrected latent space, scANVI for semi-supervised cell-type-aware embedding) — train on Perturb-seq expression matrix with guide labels as covariates → low-dimensional perturbation embeddings, UMAP visualizations, and perturbation similarity structure in latent space

Perturb-seq guide assignment: assign CRISPR gRNAs to individual cells from the single-cell Perturb-seq data (guide UMI counting and thresholding), per Replogle et al. 2022 Cell (doi:10.1016/j.cell.2022.05.013) | CRISPR guide RNA assignment to cells in a Perturb-seq single-cell screen (guide UMI counting, assignment thresholding, doublet/multiple-guide handling) → cell-by-guide assignment matrix

Perturb-seq hit calling: identify perturbations with significant gene-expression effects versus non-targeting controls, using the guide assignments from step 1 | perturbation hit calling on a Perturb-seq screen (per-perturbation differential expression vs non-targeting controls, multiple-testing correction) → ranked significant perturbation hits with effect sizes and adjusted p-values

Perturbation state modeling: build scVI/scANVI latent embedding of the Perturb-seq cells and annotate perturbation states, using the assignments and hit results from steps 1-2 | deep generative modeling of Perturb-seq single-cell expression with scVI/scANVI (perturbation labels as annotations) → latent embedding, perturbation state labels, and visualization

Perturb-seq guide assignment mapping CRISPR sgRNAs to single-cell barcodes following Replogle et al. 2022 | single-cell guide RNA assignment and cell barcode demultiplexing from Perturb-seq sequencing data → cell-to-guide mapping table and annotated single-cell count matrix

Perturbation hit calling comparing targeted cells to non-targeting control cells | phenotype scoring, statistical hit calling, and differential expression analysis between perturbed single cells and non-targeting controls → table of significant perturbation hits and effect sizes

Perturbation state representation learning and embedding using scVI and scANVI | deep generative perturbation state modeling using scVI and scANVI on single-cell perturbation expression data → latent representation embeddings and low-dimensional projection
Find and rank drug targets for myasthenia gravis

Identify tumor-reactive T cells from scRNA-seq data, including TCR clonotype analysis and exhaustion/activation marker profiling | single-cell RNA-seq analysis to identify tumor-reactive T cell populations from 10X scRNA-seq data — QC, clustering, T cell annotation, TCR VDJ clonotype integration, exhaustion/activation marker scoring, tumor-reactivity signature scoring → annotated T cell subsets with tumor-reactivity calls and TCR clonotype information

Predict neoantigens from tumor sequencing data — somatic variant calling, HLA typing, variant expression, and MHC binding affinity prediction | neoantigen prediction pipeline from tumor WES/WGS + RNA-seq — somatic variant calling (SNV/indel), HLA class I/II typing, variant expression filtering, mutant peptide binding affinity prediction (NetMHCpan/NetMHCIIpan) → ranked list of candidate neoantigens with binding affinity and expression evidence

Identify tumor-reactive T cell populations and expanded clonotypes from scRNA-seq data | single-cell phenotypic profiling and clustering of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (exhaustion markers, activation signatures, TCR clonality) → identified tumor-reactive T cell clusters

Predict tumor neoantigens and peptide-MHC binding affinities | somatic mutation-derived neoepitope identification and peptide-MHC binding affinity prediction (HLA typing, NetMHCpan/pVACtools) → ranked candidate neoantigen list

Identify tumor-reactive T cells in the user's scRNA-seq data via clustering, TCR clonotype expansion, and activation/exhaustion signature scoring | single-cell RNA-seq with VDJ/TCR repertoire analysis to identify tumor-reactive T cells — QC, clustering, T cell subset annotation, clonotype expansion analysis, and tumor-reactivity signature scoring (activation/exhaustion markers) → ranked tumor-reactive clonotypes with paired TCR sequences

Predict neoantigens and match them against the tumor-reactive TCR clonotypes from step 1 | neoantigen prediction from tumor somatic variants — HLA typing, mutant peptide generation, MHC class-I binding and immunogenicity prediction (netMHCpan/pVACseq-style) → ranked neoantigen candidates linked to TCR clonotypes

Graph-based pseudotime trajectory inference with Monocle3 (R) on the AnnData h5ad input, using the monocle_cluster and root_cell parameters | graph-based pseudotime trajectory inference on a processed single-cell AnnData object (Monocle3-style principal graph learned on a dimensionality-reduced embedding, rooted at a user-specified cell or cluster) → per-cell pseudotime values, trajectory plots (png), updated AnnData (h5ad) and per-cell metadata (csv)

RNA velocity estimation with scVelo (Python) on the same AnnData h5ad input using the specified velocity_mode | RNA velocity estimation on a single-cell AnnData object with spliced/unspliced count layers (scVelo stochastic or dynamical model, mode set by velocity_mode) → per-cell velocity vectors, velocity graph, velocity embedding stream plot (png), latent time, updated AnnData (h5ad) and per-cell metrics (csv)

Load EPIC/450K IDAT files and perform minfi functional normalisation | methylation array IDAT loading and preprocessing — minfi read.metharray.exp + functional normalisation (or noob + functional) on Illumina EPIC/450K BeadArray IDAT files → normalised beta/M values per CpG

Differential methylation analysis using DSS on normalised methylation values | differential methylation analysis with DSS (beta-binomial / Wald test on M-values or coverage) on normalised methylation data, two-group or multi-group comparison → DMRs with FDR-adjusted p-values

Gene-set enrichment analysis on differential methylation results using missMethyl | gene-set enrichment on methylation differential results using missMethyl (GO/KEGG pathway enrichment accounting for array probe bias) → enriched gene sets with FDR

IDAT → Normalisation → Differential Methylation → Gene Enrichment. EPIC/450K array methylation from IDAT — minfi load + functional normalisation, DSS differential methylation, missMethyl gene-set enrichment. Use when you want the DSS-based differential-methylation + enrichment wrapper chain. Also applicable to bismark bisulfite coverage from nf-core/methylseq.

Load raw IDAT files from EPIC/450K methylation array with minfi | import raw Illumina EPIC/450K IDAT methylation array files (minfi read.metharray) → RGChannelSet/raw methylation object with sample annotation and QC

Functional normalisation of the loaded methylation data with minfi | functional normalisation (minfi preprocessFunnorm) of EPIC/450K methylation data including probe filtering and QC → normalised beta/M-value matrix

DSS differential methylation analysis on the normalised beta values | differential methylation analysis with DSS on a normalised methylation beta-value matrix, two-group comparison → differentially methylated CpGs (DMPs) and regions (DMRs) with statistics

missMethyl gene-set enrichment on the differential methylation results | gene-set enrichment (missMethyl gometh/gsameth, array-bias-corrected) on differentially methylated CpGs/genes → enriched GO terms and KEGG pathways

Estimate human PK parameters from preclinical animal data (rat, mouse, or dog) using allometric scaling | interspecies allometric scaling and IVIVE extrapolation from preclinical animal pharmacokinetic data to predict human clearance and volume of distribution → estimated baseline human PK parameters

Full PBPK simulation with compartmental organ model and renal/hepatic impairment submodels | whole-body physiologically-based pharmacokinetic compartmental simulation with organ-specific clearances and renal/hepatic impairment submodels → plasma and tissue concentration-time curves across healthy and impaired populations

Monte Carlo population sampling for pharmacokinetic variability characterization and dose adjustment projection | population Monte Carlo simulation across physiological parameters and organ clearance distributions → virtual trial parameter distributions and recommended dose adjustments for special populations

PBPK Simulation — & Special Populations. Mechanistic PBPK simulation for predicting human pharmacokinetics from preclinical animal data. Step 1: to estimate human PK parameters from rat, mouse, or dog data. Step 2: full PBPK simulation with compartmental model and organ-specific clearance (optional renal/hepatic impairment submodel for special population dosing). Step 3: Monte Carlo sampling for variability characterization. Use for: species scaling, IND/NDA PBPK packages, first-in-human dose projection, and special population (renal/hepatic impairment) dose adjustments. Required for regulator

Estimate human PK parameters from preclinical animal data (rat, mouse, or dog) using allometric interspecies scaling for PBPK model initialization | allometric interspecies scaling of pharmacokinetic parameters (clearance, volume of distribution, half-life) from preclinical animal PK data (rat, mouse, dog) to predicted human PK parameters — power-law or exponent-based scaling → human CL, Vd, t½ estimates for PBPK model parameterization

Full mechanistic PBPK simulation with multi-compartment organ model and organ-specific clearance, with optional renal/hepatic impairment submodel for special population dosing | mechanistic whole-body PBPK simulation using multi-compartment organ-resolved physiological model with organ-specific clearance (hepatic, renal), optional renal impairment or hepatic impairment submodel for special populations — simulates plasma and tissue concentration-time profiles → PK metrics (AUC, Cmax, Tmax, trough) for standard and special populations

Monte Carlo sampling from PBPK parameter distributions to characterize inter-individual PK variability for dose optimization | Monte Carlo population PK variability simulation — sample from PBPK parameter distributions (demographics, physiology, clearance, bioavailability) across virtual population cohorts to characterize inter-individual PK variability and uncertainty → population AUC/Cmax distributions, covariate effects, dose-exposure response for IND/NDA regulatory submission

Run RNA-seq differential expression analysis to produce a ranked gene signature (up/down gene lists) | differential gene expression on bulk RNA-seq data (alignment, quantification, DESeq2/edgeR two-group comparison) → per-gene log2 fold change, adjusted p-values, and ranked gene signature for downstream connectivity analysis

Query LINCS/L1000 connectivity map with the RNA-seq differential expression signature to find drugs with matching transcriptional profiles | transcriptional signature connectivity analysis — query LINCS L1000 / CMap with a ranked gene signature (up/down gene sets from DE results) → ranked list of perturbagens (drugs/compounds) with positive and negative connectivity scores
RNA-seq processing and differential gene expression analysis | bulk RNA-seq quantification and differential expression analysis → ranked list of up- and down-regulated genes

Query reference perturbagen databases to find drugs matching the transcriptional signature | connectivity mapping of a gene expression signature against reference perturbagen profiles (LINCS L1000 / CMap) → ranked drug candidates with connectivity scores

Run RNA-seq analysis to identify differentially expressed genes (disease/treatment vs control transcriptional signature) | bulk RNA-seq processing and differential gene expression (alignment/quantification then DESeq2/edgeR-style negative-binomial model), two-group comparison → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values defining the transcriptional signature

Find drugs whose transcriptional signatures match or reverse the RNA-seq derived disease signature (LINCS L1000 connectivity mapping / signature-based drug repurposing) | signature-based drug repurposing: query a differential-expression gene signature against LINCS L1000 perturbagen connectivity-map signatures → ranked candidate compounds with connectivity scores (reversal or mimicry) and mechanism-of-action annotation

ICH S7A Phase A — CNS safety pharmacology core battery simulation: functional observational battery (FOB), locomotor activity, neuromuscular coordination (rotarod), sensory/motor reflexes, body temperature | CNS safety pharmacology simulation — functional observational battery, motor activity tracking, neuromuscular coordination assessment, autonomic and sensory-motor reflex evaluation, body temperature monitoring → CNS liability score and flagged endpoints

ICH S7A Phase B — Cardiovascular safety pharmacology core battery simulation: blood pressure (systolic/diastolic/mean), heart rate, ECG intervals (PR, QRS, QT, QTc), hERG channel liability integration | cardiovascular safety pharmacology simulation — hemodynamic monitoring (blood pressure, heart rate), ECG interval analysis (PR, QRS, QT, QTc correction), hERG liability integration → cardiovascular risk score and pro-arrhythmic flags

ICH S7A Phase C — Respiratory safety pharmacology core battery simulation: respiratory rate, tidal volume, minute volume, hemoglobin oxygen saturation, airway resistance | respiratory safety pharmacology simulation — respiratory rate, tidal volume, minute ventilation, oxygen saturation monitoring, airway resistance assessment → respiratory liability score and ventilatory depression flags

ICH S7A Phase D — Integrated safety risk assessment: combine CNS, cardiovascular, and respiratory core battery results, generate integrated safety margin analysis, NOAEL determination, secondary pharmacology cross-screen, and regulatory summary report | integrated safety pharmacology risk assessment — combine CNS, cardiovascular, and respiratory core battery outputs, compute safety margins (exposure vs NOAEL), cross-reference secondary pharmacology off-target panel, generate ICH S7A compliance summary → integrated risk report with go/no-go recommendation

Validate SMILES input file with identifier pairs | SMILES syntax and structure validation on a tabular SMILES and identifier file → validated SMILES dataset

RDKit RECAP fragmentation and decomposition into core scaffolds and R-groups | chemical fragmentation of small molecules using RDKit RECAP retrosynthetic cleavage rules → fragments, scaffolds, and R-groups

Matched molecular pair analysis using mmpdb to calculate property deltas across fragment transformations | matched molecular pair indexing and property delta computation using mmpdb on fragmented compounds → MMP transformation database with property change values

Prioritize and rank candidate scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness (QED), and synthetic accessibility (SA) score | scaffold scoring and ranking using occurrence frequency, drug-likeness descriptors (QED/Lipinski), and synthetic accessibility (SAscore) → prioritized scaffold candidate list

+ Matched Molecular Pair (MMP) pipeline Pipeline Steps: 1. — validate SMILES input file (one SMILES+ID per line) 2. — RDKit RECAP decomposition into scaffold + R-groups 3. — mmpdb : property deltas for fragment swaps 4. — rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness, SA score References: - RECAP:
Validate RNA-seq expression matrix and clinical metadata | data validation and sample alignment between RNA-seq expression count/abundance matrix and clinical metadata table

Run limma-voom transformation, linear model with covariates, eBayes moderation, and topTable extraction | differential gene expression testing using limma-voom with linear modeling and covariate adjustment → logFC, p-values, and adjusted p-values

Perform GSVA/ssGSEA gene signature scoring using MSigDB Hallmark gene sets (50 gene sets) and identify top enriched pathways per group | single-sample pathway enrichment and gene signature scoring using GSVA or ssGSEA on 50 MSigDB hallmark gene sets → per-sample enrichment matrix and group-wise comparisons

Validate SMILES input file (one SMILES+ID per line) for the Matched Molecular Pair pipeline | validation and standardization of a line-delimited SMILES+ID input file (parse with RDKit, flag invalid/duplicate structures, salt stripping) → clean validated compound table

RDKit RECAP decomposition of validated compounds into scaffolds + R-groups | RECAP retrosynthetic fragmentation of validated small molecules with RDKit → scaffold cores plus R-group fragment tables per compound

mmpdb matched molecular pair analysis: compute property deltas for fragment swaps | matched molecular pair indexing and transform extraction with mmpdb on scaffold/R-group fragments → MMP transform database with per-swap property deltas

Rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness, and synthetic accessibility (SA) score | scaffold prioritization from MMP results — rank novel scaffolds by occurrence frequency, drug-likeness (QED/Lipinski-style descriptors), and SA score → ranked scaffold hit list

Validate expression matrix and clinical metadata (sample concordance, missing values, covariate integrity) | validation and QC of a processed gene expression matrix plus clinical metadata — sample matching, missing-value and format checks → validated analysis-ready matrix and metadata table

limma-voom differential expression: voom transformation, linear model with covariates, eBayes, topTable (logFC, adj.P.Val) | differential gene expression on a processed expression matrix using limma-voom (precision weights, linear modeling with covariates, empirical Bayes moderation) → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values

GSVA/ssGSEA gene signature scoring on MSigDB hallmark collection (50 gene sets); top enriched pathways per group | gene set enrichment scoring (GSVA/ssGSEA) of a normalized expression matrix against the MSigDB hallmark collection → per-sample pathway enrichment scores and top enriched pathways per group

Validate expression matrix and clinical metadata for downstream limma-voom DE and GSVA/ssGSEA analysis | QC and validation of a pre-computed gene expression count matrix and associated clinical metadata CSV — check matrix structure, sample-to-metadata concordance, missing values, low-count filtering, and library-size normalization → validated expression matrix and cleaned sample sheet

Differential expression analysis using limma-voom: voom transformation, linear model with covariates, eBayes smoothing, topTable extraction of logFC and adj.P.Val | differential gene expression on a bulk RNA-seq count matrix using limma-voom (voom precision-weighted transformation, linear model with covariates, empirical Bayes moderation, topTable) → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values

GSVA/ssGSEA gene set enrichment on MSigDB hallmark 50 gene sets, identifying top enriched pathways per group | gene set variation analysis (GSVA/ssGSEA) on a gene expression matrix using MSigDB Hallmark 50 gene sets — compute per-sample enrichment scores, rank pathways, identify top enriched pathways per group → pathway-level enrichment score matrix and ranked pathway lists

Phase A — CNS safety pharmacology simulation: functional observational battery / modified Irwin endpoints (spontaneous locomotor activity, coordination, reflexes, body temperature) simulated from compound dose-exposure parameters | in silico central nervous system safety pharmacology assessment (functional observational battery / Irwin endpoints: motor activity, coordination, reflexes) simulated from compound exposure parameters → per-endpoint effect scores and CNS NOAEL estimate

Phase B — Cardiovascular safety pharmacology simulation: telemetry endpoints (arterial blood pressure, heart rate, ECG intervals PR/QRS/QT/QTc) simulated from compound exposure and ion-channel liability data | in silico cardiovascular safety pharmacology assessment (telemetry endpoints: blood pressure, heart rate, ECG intervals including QT/QTc) simulated from compound exposure and ion-channel data → per-endpoint effect estimates and cardiovascular NOAEL

Phase C — Respiratory safety pharmacology simulation: whole-body plethysmography endpoints (respiratory rate, tidal volume, minute ventilation) simulated from compound dose-exposure parameters | in silico respiratory safety pharmacology assessment (plethysmography endpoints: respiratory rate, tidal volume, minute ventilation) simulated from compound exposure parameters → per-endpoint effect estimates and respiratory NOAEL
